subject: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@questly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the Questly team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off a short trial focused on two key outcomes: (1) verify latency and cost against your peak 75th percentile traffic patterns, and (2) validate quality against a small closed eval set for the SearchAssist flow.

Summary / ask from Redwood
- Success criteria (your side): please confirm the top 2–3 metrics that will determine POC success (e.g., 95th latency < 350ms, top-1 relevance > 78% on eval set, acceptable fallbacks).
- Eval dataset: we need a representative sample of prompts and expected outputs (CSV is fine). Aim for ~200–500 examples for initial evaluation; include a mix of short queries, long-form prompts, and edge cases.
- Logs: if available, export 7 days of anonymized request logs (user_id replaced, timestamps retained) so we can estimate batching and cache hit rates.
- Transfer: secure S3 presigned link or SharePoint/Drive with a short-lived token; we will provide an upload target once you confirm.

Redwood commitments
- Marissa (SE) will own prompt normalization and evaluation harness setup.
- Soojin (PM) will own success criteria tracking and final acceptance checklist.
- We'll deliver an initial eval report within 10 business days of ingesting data.

Next steps
1) Alex: send sample prompts + one week of logs (anonymized) to the upload location we’ll provide.
2) Jordan: we’ll send the trial template and S3 upload instructions by EOD.
3) Align on acceptance metrics — please reply with the top 3 success metrics you want us to track.

Attachments: rdw_trial_eval_template.xlsx (empty template for mapping fields)

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com
Office: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@questly.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@questly.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. We confirm the two primary success criteria for this trial:
1) Relevance: top-1 hit rate (internal human-labeled) >= 80% on the eval set you run.
2) Latency: P95 generation time < 400ms for our baseline 512-token window under production-like QPS.

We attached a small sample (questly-prod-prompt-sample.csv) with 120 rows — a mix of search queries and assistant prompts — and a short README. We don’t have full seven days of logs ready today; Maya will export an anonymized week and upload tomorrow.

Questions:
- What exact columns should the CSV include for the eval harness? Right now we have: user_prompt, system_prompt, expected_response (optional), session_id, timestamp.
- Do you need ground-truth labels for relevance, or will Redwood run a human annotation pass?

We’ll plan to upload the full sample + logs to the link you send.

Attachments: questly-prod-prompt-sample.csv, README.txt

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of Search Product | Questly
alex.turner@questly.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@questly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan

Appreciate the prompt sample — that works well for an initial pass. Answers inline: 
- CSV columns: user_prompt (required), system_prompt (optional), expected_response (optional but helpful), label_relevance (if you have it), session_id, timestamp. If you don’t have labels, we can run a small annotation pass; tell us estimated budget for labeling (we can provide an internal cost estimate).
- Ground-truth: preferred is customer-provided if available (saves time). Otherwise Marissa will coordinate a lightweight human annotation run (we typically sample 200 items for labeling during trial).
- Upload: we’ve created a temporary S3 bucket and will send a pre-signed folder link by EOD — it will accept CSV and compressed logs (gzip). Please avoid including PII; if anything sensitive exists, mask or hash IDs.

Operational timeline (proposed):
- Day 0: Questly uploads sample CSV + anonymized logs.
- Day 1–2: Marissa ingests and normalizes prompts, runs baseline model against your sample.
- Day 3–7: Evaluation and metrics collection; if labels missing, run small annotation (3–4 days concurrently).
- Day 8–10: Deliver eval report and short recommendations (quantization/latency knobs, batch sizing).

Owners: Jordan (AE) — commercial; Marissa (SE) — evaluation; Soojin (PM) — acceptance criteria and orchestration.

Next step: Alex, please confirm you’ll upload the logs + CSV to the S3 link we send. Also confirm if you want Redwood to run the labeling pass or if Questly will provide labels.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@questly.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan

Hi Alex — quick note from the SE side with the concrete mapping we’ll use for the RDW eval harness. If you want to reduce back-and-forth, feel free to populate the attached template (rdw_trial_eval_template.xlsx) with one example row.

Required input fields (spreadsheet column names):
- example_id (string)
- user_prompt (string)
- system_prompt (string, optional)
- expected_response (string, optional)
- label_relevance (0/1 or score 0–1, optional)
- category (search | assistant | admin | other)
- anonymized_user_id
- timestamp (ISO)

If you opt for Redwood labeling: we’ll send a short questionnaire for annotators to label relevance and provide a confidence score. Labeling turnaround for 200 items typically 3 business days.

Security note: please encrypt the upload at rest; we’ll confirm the S3 bucket policy and provide a least-privilege IAM role for the transfer if needed.

I’ll start normalization as soon as files land.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@questly.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@questly.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval prompt inventory, success criteria & transfer plan

Thanks everyone — confirms plan looks good. We’ll:
- Upload full CSV (export from production) + 7-day anonymized logs to the S3 presigned path you send by EOD today.
- We’ll include label_relevance where available (~40% of rows have labels). For the remainder, Questly asks Redwood to do the annotation pass. Please provide an estimate and confirmation of labeling scope (200 items).

Acceptance: Questly will consider the trial successful if Redwood demonstrates >=80% relevance on the labeled eval set and P95 < 400ms in a production-like replay. If both are met we’ll move to a 3-month pilot cadence.

One more ask: can you include a short section in the final eval report that outlines the top 3 operational changes needed to achieve the thresholds (e.g., model variant, batch size, quantization level)? That’s helpful for our exec sponsor.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the S3 link.

Best,
Alex Turner
--- ORIGINAL ATTACHMENTS (referenced in thread) ---
questly-prod-prompt-sample.csv (120 rows)
rdw_trial_eval_template.xlsx (template with column headers)
README.txt (notes about anonymization and sampling)
